title: Reentrant localization transition, quantum butterfly and robust edge modes in aperiodic zig-zag ladder
authors: Sayan Bhattacharya, Rhiddha Acharjee, Atanu Nandy
abstract: Low dimensional tight-binding lattices in presence of quasiperiodic disorder generally exhibits localization transition. The system supports diffusive modes upto a limiting strength of disorder and all the eigenstates become localized beyond that critical strength thereby quenching the kinetic signature of the wavepacket. However, moving away from this situation, we demonstrate that with minimal long-range off-diagonal modulation, the eigenspectrum again may offer delocalization of electronic states for some subtle combination of kinetic parameters of the Hamiltonian leading to a second quantum phase change. The localization transitions are associated with the obvious presence of single-particle mobility edges. Multifractal energy landscape also shows quantum butterfly pattern with the in-gap robust edge modes. The re-emerging localization transition is manifested through the evaluation of inverse participation ratio, eigenspectrum and a pertinent quantum dynamical study.
summary: This work explores the complex electronic behavior of a quasi-one dimensional ladder lattice subjected to quasiperiodic modulation. The authors demonstrate a reentrant transition between localized and delocalized states, characterized by mobility edges. Furthermore, they identify robust edge modes whose existence is mapped onto an intriguing 'Quantum Butterfly' spectrum.
main_problem: The study investigates a reentrant localization transition, quantum butterfly pattern, and robust edge modes in an aperiodic zig-zag ladder structure.
main_result: The system exhibits a re-emerging delocalization phase controlled by kinetic parameters, confirmed by mobility edges, alongside the observation of stable edge states resistant to moderate disorder.
method: Analysis involves calculating spectral properties using Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), studying transport dynamics via Mean Square Displacement (MSD), and mapping energy spectra onto a quantum butterfly structure.
model_or_system: The model is a quasi-one dimensional zig-zag ladder network governed by a tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating a quasiperiodic Aubry-Andre Harper (AAH) modulation in the long-range hopping integral.
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio ($	ext{IPR}_n$), Normalized Participation Ratio ($	ext{NPR}_n$), Mean Square Displacement (MSD), Edge Probability ($P_{	ext{edge}}$), and Transport Exponent ($\mu$).
important_parameters: Slowness exponent ($\alpha$), hopping strengths ($t, \lambda_0$), disorder strength ($W_d$), and modulation frequency ($ eta$ set to the golden mean).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that multifractal methods are applicable to characterize the energy landscape in this quasiperiodic model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate IPR intensity plots showing re-entrant transitions, phase diagrams mapping delocalized/localized regimes ($\eta$), MSD curves characterizing transport exponents ($\mu$), and probability density maps distinguishing edge vs. bulk states on the quantum butterfly spectrum.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes localization diagnostics (IPR, $	ext{NPR}$) to find a re-entrant transition controlled by $\alpha$. It then uses dynamical studies (MSD) for confirmation, explores multifractality and the 'Quantum Butterfly' structure, and finally isolates robust edge modes using edge probability analysis.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed diagnostics—combining spectral measures (IPR), transport dynamics ($\mu$), and geometric features (butterfly)—to map out complex phase transitions in quasiperiodic systems, which is highly relevant for understanding localization phenomena beyond simple disorder models.
